description.value: The study investigated neural representations of a signal-detection-theory decision variable and perceptual confidence during visual motion discrimination, and tested whether cortical decision-variable signals are linked to striatal confidence signals.

design.value: Nineteen young neurologically healthy subjects performed a visual random-dot motion discrimination task during fMRI, reporting a binary motion-direction choice followed by a continuous confidence rating; one participant was excluded for excessive head motion, leaving 18 subjects. The study used mass-univariate fMRI analysis, multivariate searchlight classification, multivariate searchlight regression, and multivariate connectivity analysis.

description.value: Subjects rated confidence of the judgment on a continuous scale by moving a white dot with a trackball to the part of the confidence bar corresponding to their confidence.
A binary perceptual judgment of the dominant direction of motion of the stimulus, motion up or motion down.
Behavioral accuracy of the perceptual motion-direction judgment.
Response time during the perceptual decision task.

source_definition.value: The degree to which we believe in the accuracy of our percepts.

A proxy of the difference between the decision variable and the criterion, constructed on each trial as the binary choice coded as -1 or 1 multiplied with the binned confidence rating coded as 0.5, 1.5, and 2.5.
Response time was used as a parametric regressor to account for variance in BOLD signal amplitude.
Six additional head motion regressors were included.

description.value: Nineteen young and neurologically healthy subjects took part in the study; one participant was subsequently excluded due to excessive head motion, leaving 18 subjects (6 female, 1 left-handed, mean age: 26.4 years, SD: 3.4).

task_description.value: Subjects observed a random dot motion stimulus and performed two consecutive responses: a binary perceptual judgment of the dominant direction of motion and a rating of confidence of the judgment on a continuous scale.

instructions.value: Subjects were instructed to respond even when they were very unsure; the confidence scale ranged from very sure about the direction of motion to no idea at all.

stimuli.value: Random dot motion stimulus in which an individually calibrated percentage of dots moved either upward or downward while all other dots moved in random directions; motion coherence was fixed to the 75% threshold of each subject.

task_description.value: A functional localizer run was used to locate motion-sensitive region MT+/V5 in each individual subject.

instrument.value: 3.0 Tesla TIM Trio MRI (Siemens) and a 12-channel head coil

description.value: T2*-weighted gradient-echo echo-planar images were acquired; 2247 functional volumes were acquired per subject, corresponding to the experimental runs and the functional localizer.

Functional images were spatially realigned and slice-timing corrected. For the univariate analysis, images were spatially normalized using the DARTEL transformation matrix and smoothed with a Gaussian kernel of 6 mm FWHM. For both multivariate analyses, functional data were not spatially warped or smoothed.

steps.value: creation of a template structural reference image using DARTEL
affine transformation of the template to MNI space
6 mm FWHM Gaussian smoothing for univariate analysis
no spatial warping or smoothing for multivariate analyses

model_settings.value: Ten regressors per run; stimulation regressor modeled with a 2-s boxcar at random-dot-motion stimulus onset; confidence entered as a parametric modulator; missed trials, six head-motion regressors, a constant term, and a 1/128-Hz high-pass filter were included.
Searchlight sphere radius 10 mm; leave-one-run-out cross-validation; classification separately for each motion direction; standard cost value c = 1; group-level t-test against 50% chance accuracy.

Searchlight sphere radius 10 mm; six decision-variable regressors per run; 30 pattern vectors; labels ranged from -2.5 to 2.5; nu = 0.5 and c = 1; predictions were evaluated by Fisher-z-transformed correlations; results were masked by choice-related regions.

Predicted decision-variable labels from 12 candidate seed regions were transformed into predicted confidence values and correlated with predicted confidence in the ventral striatum across runs; 120 run permutations per subject were used, with Bonferroni correction across 12 regions.

name.value: Negative parametric effect related to confidence

definition.value: Negative linear relationship between the BOLD signal amplitude and the confidence of the subject across all experimental runs.

model_representation_notes.value: The GLM included a stimulation regressor, a confidence parametric modulator, a missed-trials regressor, six head-motion regressors, a constant term, and a 1/128-Hz high-pass filter.

interpretations.value: Brain regions exhibiting decreases in BOLD signal with increasing confidence.

definition.value: Brain regions where patterns of brain activity predicted the subject's decision and their associated confidence; the decision variable was reconstructed by multiplying the binary choice by the binned confidence rating.

name.value: correlation between true labels and labels predicted from the regression model

model_representation_notes.value: The analysis used a linear support vector regression model with nu = 0.5 and c = 1; six decision-variable regressors were modeled per run, corresponding to three confidence levels for each of two choices.

interpretations.value: Activity patterns in several predominantly frontal and parietal brain regions reflected the perceptual decision variable.

name.value: positive parametric effect related to confidence

definition.value: Positive linear relationship between the BOLD signal amplitude and the confidence of the subject across all experimental runs.

model_representation_notes.value: The GLM included a stimulation regressor, a confidence parametric modulator, a missed-trials regressor, six head-motion regressors, a constant term, and a 1/128-Hz high-pass filter.

interpretations.value: Activity in the ventral striatum around the nucleus accumbens increased with the level of confidence.

title.value: Brain regions where activity is related to confidence

caption.value: A complete list of brain regions with parametric increases and decreases in brain activity in relationship to confidence. The coordinates and z-values refer to the peak within each cluster. Results are reported at P < 0.0001, corrected family-wise for cluster size at P < 0.05.

description.value: Reports brain regions with parametric increases and decreases in brain activity in relationship to confidence.

title.value: Brain regions informative about the DV

caption.value: Brain regions carrying information about the DV reconstructed from choices and confidence ratings. Mean Fisher z-values reflect the z-transformed size of the correlation between predicted and true values in the multivariate regression analysis. The coordinates, mean Fisher z-values, and statistical z-values of the normal distribution refer to the peak within each cluster. Results are reported at P < 0.0001, corrected family-wise for cluster size at P < 0.05.

description.value: Reports brain regions carrying information about the decision variable reconstructed from choices and confidence ratings.
